config.text: Studio product photograph, top-down, of one single tall narrow vertical menu card, very elongated proportion of 10 by 21 centimetres, lying flat and centred on a pale warm grey linen tablecloth, soft even daylight, the whole card visible with margin around it. The card is thick uncoated deep burgundy cotton paper, colour sang-de-boeuf #560002. The only printing is hot-foil stamping in two flat layers: underneath, a salmon in flat opaque matte white foil; on top, a lamb in flat bright silver metallic foil, printed over the white and fully opaque where they overlap. Each foil is one perfectly uniform solid area with crisp edges and a slight debossed relief in the paper. Drawing language of contemporary independent illustration posters: bold flat silhouettes, a few confident cut lines inside the shapes that reveal the burgundy paper, each cut line at least as thick as a pencil stroke; wild, expressive, slightly menacing creatures with dynamic twisted bodies, sharp and adult, with dry humour. The card carries no lettering. Relationship and composition: the lamb and the salmon wrestle, their bodies twisted into one compact knot that fills the whole card, the lamb's legs wrapped around the fish, the salmon's body bent around the lamb's neck. Flat figures with thin white-to-burgundy cut lines marking muscles and joints, in the manner of flat black-and-white mythological fight scenes.
